contexts.text: No one is ever rewarded (there) for good acts, if he has placed merit in them...
No one is rewarded on account of his doing good, and teaching truth.
When (the spiritual man) does good to anyone... he thinks of reward, either from them, or from the Lord.
Whereas he who acts from affection... having the reward in the delight, does not think of merit.

Those who are in good, are in the affection of doing good for the sake of the good, and this without reward to them: their reward is that they are allowed to do what is good... But those who are in truth... for the most part think of reward...
The Lord demands from man humiliation, adoration, etc., which appear like repayings. Explained.
Issachar = reward from works. (See Issachar.) AC 6388:2.

Those who do good for the sake of reward, do indeed perform uses, and are of service, but are among those in the Lord's Kingdom who are in the lowest place; for they do not dispense the good which is communicated to them, except towards those who can recompense them, and pass by the rest, who need aid the most; or, if they do good to these, it is from the end of reward by the Lord... They thus recede from humiliation, and, in the same proportion, from a state of reception of happiness...
Works of good without reward: that they are full of happiness. Signified, Explained.
No others are in these things, which are signified by rest or peace, than those who are in the good of charity, thus in works of good without reward.
They who do goods merely from the end of reward, cannot possibly know that in doing goods without reward, the happiness is so great that it is heavenly happiness. (The reason explained.)

Such do not believe that there can be any delight in doing good without the end of reward; for they suppose that if there is no end of reward, all delight ceases; and if they are told further that when this delight ceases heavenly delight begins, they are amazed... AC 6392:2, Explained.
Pleasant = the happiness which is in works of good without reward.
That those have Heaven who do good without an end of reward. Illustrated.

As soon as the thought occurs that he wills to communicate what he has for the sake of obtaining that influx of blessedness, the influx is dissipated; and still more so if there presents itself any thought about a reward from him to whom he communicates his good.
Truth is falsified when it is said that all the good which man does... is done for the sake of reward, and that therefore works of charity are not to be done.
Charity is an internal affection, which consists in... wanting to do good to the neighbour... and this without reward.
They do not comprehend that to want to do good to the neighbour without reward is Heaven in man... AC 8462:end.
Hence to every good there has been adjoined its reward.
He knows from doctrine that charity is not to do good for the sake of reward...
The man of the External Church does truth and good... that he may be rewarded, and therefore in the truth and good he does there is the idea of self...
It is a law of Divine order that good has in it the reward, thus Heaven. AC 9049.
The affection of charity is to communicate goods without the end of reward; but no affection of charity is to communicate goods for the sake of a reward as the end. Illustrated, References.
To give silver to usury = to teach for the sake of gain only, thus to do good for the sake of reward.
The goods which men do from themselves are not goods, because they are done for the sake of self, because for the sake of the reward...

To believe that they will be rewarded if they do good, is not hurtful with those who are in innocence... But to confirm themselves in it when they become adults, is hurtful. For man is initiated into good by looking to the reward.
Order cannot be maintained without governors... who must reward those who live according to order.
Unless (men) were held in bonds... by rewards suited to their loves, which are honours and gains for those who do goods; and by punishments... the human race would perish.
For he who wants to merit, wants to be rewarded.
Natural charity is a working for favour, for the sake of some reward.
Each (officer), according to the extent of his duty, and the goods of use he performs, has remuneration...
They are not rewarded from merit, but from mercy.
Mutual love rewards itself.
If (this cutter of wood) thought, spoke, or acted, well, he wanted to be rewarded; so that reward was in every single thing.
The Lord leads them... by rewards in the world.
There everyone is rewarded according to the excellence of the use, and at the same time according to the affection for the use.

The Lord moves the wicked to do good to others... but the man is not rewarded for it. But if a man does good... from a spiritual affection, he is rewarded. His reward is the heavenly delight of that affection.
